published.citation: computed from wolf-327's temperature, 3542 K, and the orbit's a/R* 5.3, as T* (R*/a)^(1/2) (2/3)^(1/4): 1390 K; the source gives no uncertainty, so the range is the value itself, https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06573

temperature.note: Nobody has measured its heat or imaged it; this is the hottest day side a dark, airless rock can have on its orbit, an estimate, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: the bare-rock maximum, no light reflected and no heat carried to the night side; the star's temperature is Murgas et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Wolf 327 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive, a/R* is Murgas et al. 2024
